subject: radiology
title: Boot Shaped Heart, Egg on String and Snowman Signs

steps.title: Boot shape means Fallot physiology
steps.tx: **Boot shaped heart**, the coeur en sabot, combines an upturned cardiac apex with a concave pulmonary bay. Right ventricular hypertrophy lifts the apex upward like a boot toe, while the narrowed right ventricular outflow and small pulmonary artery hollow out the left upper border. The same film shows pulmonary oligaemia, so the boot plus dark lung fields in a cyanosed child names tetralogy of Fallot before echocardiography.
steps.say: Boot shaped heart combines an upturned apex with a concave pulmonary bay. Right ventricular hypertrophy lifts the apex like a boot toe, while the narrowed outflow hollows the left upper border. Dark oligaemic lung fields beside the boot in a cyanosed child name tetralogy of Fallot before echocardiography.

steps.title: Four defects behind the boot
steps.tx: **Tetralogy components** are a ventricular septal defect, an overriding aorta, right ventricular outflow obstruction and right ventricular hypertrophy. The film only shows two of them directly: the hypertrophy lifting the apex and the small pulmonary artery emptying the bay. Severity follows the outflow obstruction, because tighter obstruction drives more right to left shunt, deeper cyanosis and earlier presentation in the newborn period.

steps.title: Congenital film patterns compared
steps.tx: **Cardiac silhouettes** on paediatric chest films compress complex anatomy into named shapes that examiners love. The pictured set lines up classic silhouettes beside their vascularity, separating cyanotic lesions with oligaemia from those with plethora. Reading shape and lung blood flow together halves the differential before any measurement: boot with dark lungs is Fallot, snowman with wet lungs is anomalous pulmonary venous return.

steps.title: Egg on string in transposition
steps.tx: **Egg on string sign** shows an egg shaped heart lying on its side with a narrow string like superior mediastinum in transposition of the great arteries. The narrow pedicle appears because the aorta and pulmonary artery stack front to back instead of side by side, losing their normal width, and thymic stress involution thins it further. Pulmonary plethora completes the picture in a deeply cyanosed newborn.

The pedicle narrows because aorta and pulmonary artery stack front to back, losing normal width. Pulmonary plethora completes the picture in a deeply cyanosed newborn.

steps.title: Snowman from anomalous veins
steps.tx: **Snowman sign**, also called figure of eight, forms in supracardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous connection. The dilated vertical vein, innominate vein and superior vena cava build the snowman head above an enlarged heart forming the body. All four pulmonary veins drain into that channel instead of the left atrium, so the right heart carries the entire venous return and the lungs show plethora with pulmonary oedema when obstructed.

All four pulmonary veins drain into that channel instead of the left atrium, so the right heart carries the entire venous return.

steps.tx: The **snowman sign**, also called the figure of eight, forms in supracardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous connection. The dilated vertical vein, innominate vein, and superior vena cava make the head, and an enlarged heart makes the body. All four pulmonary veins drain into that channel instead of the left atrium, so the right heart carries the entire venous return. The lungs look plethoric. Pulmonary oedema appears when the anomalous pathway is obstructed.
steps.say: Supracardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous connection produces the snowman sign. The vertical vein, innominate vein, and superior vena cava form the head over an enlarged heart. All four pulmonary veins use that route rather than the left atrium, so the right heart takes the whole venous return, and obstruction brings oedema.

steps.title: Figure of three and rib notching
steps.tx: **Figure of 3 sign** outlines the aorta in coarctation: the dilated segment above the narrowing, the waist at the coarctation and the post stenotic dilatation below stack into a figure three on the frontal film. The same obstruction erodes the inferior borders of the third to eighth ribs, where enlarged intercostal collaterals pulse against bone. Rib notching spares the first two ribs because their arteries arise above the narrowing.
steps.say: Figure of three sign outlines the aorta in coarctation: dilatation above, the waist at the narrowing and dilatation below stack into a three. The same obstruction erodes the inferior borders of ribs three to eight, where enlarged collaterals pulse against bone. The first two ribs are spared because their arteries arise above.

steps.title: Water bottle and egg shapes in adults
steps.tx: **Water bottle heart** describes the flask shaped, globally enlarged silhouette of a large pericardial effusion, with sharp borders because fluid, not myocardium, sets the edge. The heart still shows a normal cardiothoracic shape inside on echocardiography. In adults an egg shaped calcified mass beside the heart instead suggests a pericardial cyst or loculated effusion, and tamponade physiology, not silhouette size, decides the urgency of drainage.
steps.say: Water bottle heart describes the flask shaped enlarged silhouette of a large pericardial effusion, with sharp borders because fluid sets the edge. Echocardiography still shows a normal shaped heart inside. Tamponade physiology, not silhouette size, decides the urgency of drainage when pressure rises.

steps.title: Plethora versus oligaemia sorts cyanosis
steps.tx: **Pulmonary vascularity** is the second half of every congenital film read. Plethora shows enlarged central and peripheral vessels reaching the outer third of lung in left to right shunts and transposition. Oligaemia shows small hila and dark, underfilled lungs in Fallot and pulmonary atresia. Pairing vascularity with silhouette separates lesions that share cyanosis: egg on string is wet, boot is dry, and that split drives the first echocardiography questions.
steps.say: Pulmonary vascularity is the second half of every congenital film read. Plethora shows enlarged vessels reaching the outer third in left to right shunts and transposition. Oligaemia shows small hila and dark underfilled lungs in Fallot. Egg on string is wet, boot is dry, and that split drives the first echo questions.
